facts: At the bottom of the Mariana Trench the pressure is over one thousand times what you feel at the surface: roughly a small car balanced on your thumbnail.
Anglerfish carry their own biological lanterns, powered by bioluminescent bacteria that live inside the lure.
More of the ocean floor remains unmapped in detail than the surface of Mars.
Sunlight gives up at about one thousand metres down. Below that lies the midnight zone, where most light is made by the animals themselves.
An estimated three quarters of deep sea animals can produce their own light.
The glass squid is almost perfectly transparent, except for its eyes, which cast the only shadow a predator might spot.
Sperm whales dive more than two kilometres deep and can hold their breath for over an hour while hunting squid in the dark.
When a whale dies and sinks, the carcass, called a whale fall, can feed an entire ecosystem on the seafloor for decades.
The deep sea is Earth's largest habitat by volume, and most species living there have never been given a name.
Giant squid have the largest eyes in the animal kingdom, the size of dinner plates, tuned to catch the faintest glow.
Hydrothermal vents host animals that never rely on sunlight at all: their food chain starts with chemicals dissolved in scalding water.
Some deep sea sharks glow faintly on their undersides, hiding their silhouette from anything looking up.
